summary: Added or reconsulted eight expert, curricular, review and reader sources. Logged disagreement over canon boundaries and kept educational sequence distinct from ranking.
next: Add independently authored scholarly book reviews and blogs; broaden source domains.

sources.title: Key Philosophical Texts in the Western Canon
sources.author: Nigel Warburton; interviewed by Sophie Roell
sources.note: Warburton selects classics partly for accessibility and literary qualities. His five choices are explicitly Western and all male; Republic is discussed through ethics and political analogy.

targets.B: Offers a stated selection rationale, not universal merit positions.
targets.P: Provides reception evidence for Plato, Descartes, Hume, Mill and Wittgenstein.

sources.limits: Narrow Western selection; introductory accessibility is distinct from greatest-ever merit.

sources.title: The Best Philosophy Books by Women
sources.author: Lisa Whiting and Rebecca Buxton; interviewed by Nigel Warburton
sources.note: The interview questions how canons exclude women and selects Davis, Manne, Midgley, Shklar and Benhabib. It distinguishes a book about philosophers from an anthology of their texts.

targets.A: Broadens political, feminist and citizenship book candidates.
targets.N: Adds social-critical nonfiction by five women.
targets.B: Adds distinct ethical and political arguments omitted from male-only lists.
targets.P: Documents canon exclusion and specific overlooked philosophers.

sources.limits: One jointly authored selection, not five independent sources; shared interviewer with other Five Books pieces.

sources.title: The best books on Philosophy in the Islamic World
sources.author: Peter Adamson; interviewed by Nigel Warburton
sources.note: Adamson distinguishes language, ethnicity, religion and political setting. He recommends studies of Greek-Arabic transmission, Avicenna, Maimonides and al-Razi, rejecting a simple Golden-Age endpoint.
candidates: Avicenna's De Anima in the Latin West
The Teleological Ethics of Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

targets.A: Adds intellectual history across languages and religious communities.
targets.B: Adds philosophical monographs and a scope correction for Islamic-world thought.
targets.P: Supports cross-community reception of Avicenna, Maimonides and al-Razi.

sources.limits: Recommended books are secondary scholarship; do not imply they are primary texts by the studied philosophers.

sources.title: The best books on World Philosophy
sources.author: Bryan Van Norden; interviewed by Nigel Warburton
sources.note: Van Norden pairs Plato and Hume with Mengzi, Zhuangzi and Shantideva, arguing that academic access and exclusion shape the apparent canon.

targets.A: Adds a comparative cross-tradition reading selection.
targets.N: Supports Hume and canon-history nonfiction; hybrid texts retain genre flags.
targets.B: Supplies named Chinese and Indian philosophical classics alongside European ones.
targets.P: Challenges equating departmental representation with worldwide philosophical merit.

sources.limits: Interview's historical claims require independent corroboration; linked editorial is an uncounted lead.
sources.dependency_note: The interview explicitly develops the author's joint New York Times editorial and Taking Back Philosophy; not independent votes for those same arguments.

sources.title: Who Is The Best Philosopher?
sources.note: Reader submissions disagree about the best philosopher and proposed standards. One Hume submission distinguishes communication, breadth and lasting contribution and cites Think and Kant's first Critique.

targets.A: Adds reader reception for philosophical nonfiction and a warning about incompatible standards.
targets.N: Records reader reasons for valuing Think and critical philosophy.
targets.B: Adds criterion disagreement without adopting any proposed standard.
targets.P: Direct evidence of disagreement among readers about philosopher comparisons.

sources.limits: Edited reader submissions count once; subjective reasons, not a representative poll.

sources.title: Recommended Reads
sources.note: Mini-reviews distinguish accessible introductions from advanced surveys. Ayer's twentieth-century account is criticized for limited Continental coverage; Magee's interview anthology supplies historical entry points.

targets.A: Adds nonfiction philosophy introductions and criticism of coverage.
targets.B: Distinguishes introductory teaching usefulness from comprehensive philosophical history.
targets.P: Shows a familiar selection of Plato, Descartes, Heidegger, Hume and Wittgenstein in public pedagogy.

sources.limits: Historical reviews and prices are not current buying guidance; one review admits partial reading.

sources.title: Introduction to Political Philosophy
sources.author: Steven B. Smith
sources.note: The syllabus groups political texts around city-state, sovereignty, constitutional government and democracy. Sessions assign parts of works, so teaching order is neither complete-book coverage nor rank.

targets.N: Adds political nonfiction across historical institutional questions.
targets.B: Connects named primary texts to specific political-philosophy problems.
targets.P: Documents curricular reception of Plato, Aristotle, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau and Tocqueville.

sources.location: Course description, texts and session list
sources.limits: Western introductory syllabus; lecture videos not watched or counted separately.

sources.title: St. John's Reading List: A Great Books Curriculum
sources.note: The curriculum links Aristotle's ethical and natural works, Euclid's Elements, Harvey's circulation treatise and Herodotus's Histories. It warns that selections and campus lists vary.
candidates: On the Motion of the Heart and Blood in Animals

targets.N: Adds mathematics, medicine and history rather than treating nonfiction as only philosophy.
targets.B: Documents teaching use of Aristotle's philosophical and scientific texts.
targets.P: Provides curricular reception of Aristotle; not every listed scientist is a philosopher.

sources.limits: A Western educational collection; extracts and sequence must not acquire merit positions.
